Quality, Compliance, Performance, Safeguarding and MI teams

Participants (young people aged 18 to 24) and, where appropriate and with consent, their support networks

Jobcentre Plus, local authorities, education and training providers

Activity Design and Delivery

Design, coordinate and maintain a rolling programme of structured group and individual activities aligned with participants needs, aspirations, action plans and outcomes.

Deliver welcoming, energetic and inclusive sessions for young people aged 18 to 24, using age-appropriate interests such as sport, creative arts, technology, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor activities and community projects.

Prepare clear session plans, learning objectives, resources and contingency arrangements so every activity supports employability, personal development or progression.

Adapt pace, content and delivery for different communication styles, neurodiversity, disabilities, literacy levels, digital capability, confidence levels and reasonable-adjustment needs.

Participant Engagement and Development

Use trauma-informed, strengths-based and culturally responsive practice to build trust, promote participant choice and voice, and support those who lack confidence or have had negative experiences of services or education.

Provide practical sector insight through employer talks, workplace visits, careers activities, mock recruitment exercises, volunteering and project-based learning.

title: Youth Mentoring Coordinator
description:
Hours: 37.5 hours per week (full-time)
Contract: 3-year fixed-term contract

Location: Milton Keynes

We're delighted to be partnering with the National Lottery Community Fund as part of our Youth Mentoring MK project. Their funding and support means we're able to expand our mentoring support for children and young people across Milton Keynes, helping those experiencing poverty, disadvantage and discrimination to build confidence, improve their wellbeing and achieve their goals.

We're looking for a passionate, organised and motivated Youth Mentoring Coordinator to help young people build confidence, develop resilience and make positive choices about their future.

You'll play an important role in delivering our community-based mentoring programme, working directly with young people while recruiting, supporting and coordinating a team of volunteer mentors who share our commitment to making a difference.

This is a role for someone who loves working with young people, enjoys bringing people together and wants to create meaningful, lasting impact in their community.

The opportunity

We believe every young person deserves to feel supported, valued and able to reach their potential, whatever challenges they may face.

As our Youth Mentoring Coordinator, you'll help deliver a mentoring programme that provides young people with positive role models, trusted relationships and practical support to navigate life's challenges.

You'll work directly with young people who may be experiencing difficulties with their emotional wellbeing, relationships, education or personal circumstances, helping them recognise their strengths, set achievable goals and move towards a more positive future.

You'll also coordinate our volunteer mentors, ensuring they feel confident, supported and equipped to make a real difference.

From recruiting and welcoming new volunteers to matching them with opportunities, providing ongoing guidance and monitoring the quality of mentoring, you'll help create a positive experience for both mentors and young people.

You'll work closely with community organisations, local partners and the wider YMCA team to ensure young people can access the right support and opportunities.

Above all, you'll help create the trusted relationships and consistent support that can change the direction of a young person's life.

What you'll be doing

You'll play a hands-on role in coordinating and delivering our community-based youth mentoring programme.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Building positive, trusting relationships with young people and providing tailored one-to-one mentoring and support.
- Assessing young people's individual needs and developing person-centred mentoring plans with clear, achievable goals.
- Supporting young people to build confidence, resilience, emotional wellbeing, positive relationships and essential life skills.
- Managing a caseload of young people with medium to high levels of risk or support needs, ensuring appropriate safeguarding and support arrangements are in place.
- Recruiting, coordinating and supporting a team of volunteer mentors, helping them feel confident, motivated and equipped to succeed.
- Providing guidance and ongoing support to volunteers, overseeing mentoring activities, session records and safeguarding practices.
- Coordinating volunteer rotas, placements and activities to ensure effective delivery of mentoring services.
- Building positive relationships with community organisations, referral partners and other local services.
- Connecting young people with additional support and opportunities, including wider YMCA services where appropriate.
- Monitoring mentoring outcomes, maintaining accurate records and demonstrating the positive impact of the programme.
- Working collaboratively with colleagues and partners to develop and improve mentoring services for young people across Milton Keynes.

Just as importantly, you'll create an environment where young people feel heard, volunteers feel valued and everyone understands the difference their contribution makes.

About you

We're looking for someone who genuinely cares about young people and believes in the power of positive relationships to change lives.

You'll have experience working with young people, understand the challenges they may face and be confident providing support that is compassionate, practical and tailored to their individual needs.

You'll also enjoy working with volunteers, helping people feel welcomed, supported and motivated to give their best.

You don't need to have held a formal management position, but you will need to be organised, confident coordinating others and comfortable taking responsibility for the effective delivery of mentoring activities.

You'll be someone who:
- Has experience working directly with young people in youth work, mentoring, education, community services or a similar setting.
- Understands the emotional, social and developmental needs of young people.
- Can build positive, trusting relationships with young people from different backgrounds.
- Has experience coordinating, supervising or supporting volunteers, colleagues or others delivering activities.
- Is organised, reliable and confident managing competing priorities and responsibilities.
- Can assess individual needs, develop support plans and monitor progress.
- Understands safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries and the importance of managing risk.
- Communicates effectively with young people, volunteers, colleagues and external partners.
- Is compassionate, resilient and able to respond positively to challenging situations.
- Enjoys developing relationships, bringing people together and helping others succeed.
- Takes ownership, follows things through and looks for ways to improve how services are delivered.
- Brings enthusiasm, initiative and a genuine commitment to helping young people thrive.

Experience supporting young people affected by trauma, instability, youth offending or other complex challenges would be particularly valuable.

Experience recruiting, training or coordinating volunteers within a charity, community or youth organisation would also be an advantage.

A relevant degree-level qualification in youth work, social work, education, social sciences or a related field would be beneficial but isn't essential.

Why Join YMCA South Midlands?

Because this is an opportunity to make a genuine difference, not just to the young people we support, but to the volunteers who give their time to help others.

You'll join an organisation that believes in the potential of every young person and the power of strong communities to create positive change.

As part of our Youth & Community team, you'll have the opportunity to:
- Build meaningful relationships and help young people overcome challenges and achieve their potential.
- Recruit, support and develop a committed team of volunteer mentors.
- Play an important role in delivering and improving our community-based mentoring programme.
- Work with local organisations and partners to create more opportunities for young people.
- Be part of a supportive, collaborative team that genuinely cares about making a difference.
- See the positive impact of your work on young people, volunteers and the wider community.

Everyone is Welcome Here

At YMCA South Midlands, we believe everyone should feel they belong.

We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and communities. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the people we serve and where everyone is treated with dignity, respect and fairness.

As a charity with a Christian heritage, our faith inspires our values and our commitment to serving others. We welcome people of all faiths and none. All appointments are made on merit.

Safeguarding

YMCA South Midlands is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. The successful candidate will be required to complete appropriate safer recruitment checks, including an enhanced DBS check and a children's barred list check where the role is eligible.

Reasonable Adjustments

We want every candidate to have the opportunity to perform at their best throughout our recruitment process.

If you have a disability, long-term health condition or are neurodivergent and would benefit from any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know when you apply or contact us at any stage. We'll be happy to discuss how we can support you.

A note to recruitment agencies: We are managing recruitment for this role directly and are not seeking support from recruitment agencies. Please do not submit speculative CVs or contact us regarding this vacancy.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Ashfield Medical Centre is a very busy and friendly GP Practice in Milton Keynes. We are currently looking to add to our fabulous reception team with a morning receptionist. Hours to be worked at 7am till 1pm Monday to Friday (with the possibility of overtime covering the afternoon shift of 1pm till 7pm as required). We would prefer that you have experience of working within a GP Practice environment or previous NHS experience and working knowledge of Systm1 but full training can be provided in any case for the right candidate. Starting salary £13.00 per hour rising to £13.25 per hour after successful completion of the probationary period and training. Key skills required for the role included face to face engagement with the public, excellent telephone manner, clear and precise typing and writing, ability to work on own or as part of a team, knowledge of medical terminology and ability to raise prescriptions ready for electronic signing. Out reception team also work as chaperones when required for the GPs and Nursing Team. All necessary training will be provided. This list is not exhaustive. Job summary: The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the senior receptionist/practice manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Opening up/locking-up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Filing and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Clearing and re-stock consulting rooms as required Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required; loading and emptying the dishwasher and keeping the kitchen area clean and tidy Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Any other delegated duties appropriate to the post Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance
